answer: Operator-Linked Identity Expansion. Each new wallet must declare a parent operator; identities form a grove, and when one wallet is caught, every sibling under that operator is frozen for 30 days and loses 10% of its transaction throughput. Costs the attacker a whole operator lineage, not a throwaway wallet — a fresh spiral of identities means rebuilding reputation from zero. Disputes escalate to a lagoon of staked auditors who resolve within 72 hours; a false freeze costs the accuser their own throughput cut.
